lessons.title: 1. Meet C++
lessons.description: Welcome! Let's take your first steps into programming. C++ programs are simple instructions your computer follows to display text, solve math, and build software.
learning_objectives: Recognize a C++ program and print text using std::cout

exercises.question: What does a computer program do?
options: It gives step-by-step instructions for the computer to follow
It physically cleans the computer processor
It makes the internet faster automatically
exercises.correct_answer: It gives step-by-step instructions for the computer to follow
exercises.explanation: Programs are sequence of instructions written in code!

exercises.question: In C++, `std::cout` prints the value of what follows it. What will `std::cout << 7 + 5;` display?
exercises.explanation: std::cout evaluates the expression and prints the result, so 7 + 5 shows 12.

exercises.question: Complete the C++ line to print 'C++': std::cout << ___ ;
exercises.explanation: Text in C++ is wrapped in double quotes.

exercises.title: Return C++ string
exercises.question: Return the string "C++" from get_language().

mastery_exam.question: Which C++ command displays output to the terminal?
mastery_exam.explanation: std::cout is C++ standard output stream; std::cin reads input instead.

mastery_exam.question: Fill in the symbol that ends a C++ statement: int x = 5___
mastery_exam.explanation: Every C++ statement ends with a semicolon.

source.name: cppreference.com — std::cout — global object controlling output to stdout

lessons.title: 2. Integers & Arithmetic
lessons.description: In C++, integer calculations use fundamental types like `int`. Implement `calculate_total(int price, int quantity)`.
learning_objectives: Use int primitive arithmetic in C++

source.name: cppreference.com — Fundamental types — int, basic integer type

lessons.title: 3. Rocket Payload Fuel Calculator
lessons.description: Calculate required rocket fuel mass in C++: fuel equals `payload_mass * distance * 0.15`.
learning_objectives: Combine double variables and floating point math in C++

exercises.question: Each declaration below is meant to end up holding 2.5. Select every one that actually does.
exercises.explanation: `5 / 2` is integer division and yields 2 before the double ever sees it, and `int w` truncates the 2.5 it is given. One operand written as a decimal is enough to make the division floating-point.

lessons.title: 4. Circle Area Calculator (Practice)
lessons.description: Calculate circle area using pi * radius * radius.

lessons.title: 5. Section 1 Checkpoint: C++ Foundations Mastery
lessons.description: Checkpoint for variables and arithmetic: implement square(int x) returning x * x. The test asserts square(6) == 36.

mastery_exam.question: Which C++ statement includes the string library?
mastery_exam.explanation: #include <string> pulls in std::string; iostream is for streams.

mastery_exam.question: Complete the C++ main function return: return ___;
mastery_exam.explanation: main returns 0 to signal success to the operating system.
